cells.place: Pāṇḍya
cells.language: Sanskrit and Tamil, Grantha and Vaṭte-luttu.
cells.remarks: Issued from Kakkūdi. States that while king Varaguns, was ruling, two villages, Tirumangalam and Somaküriśēri clubbed together into one were granted by the king (Paran-takap-Virapāṇḍayanan) to several Brahmans at the instance of Nīlakaṇṭhan-Kēśavan of the chōli (brāhmaṇa) of Tirumangalam. States also that Kachugön, a predecessor of the king, who uprooted the Kalappālar had granted the village of 12 vėlis of land to 12 Brahmans and the latter to Käthakamasavājin and that subsequently the same village was occupied by Kadattirukkai-kilavan. Cf. Tamil text published in Tamil Pōli, Vol. XXXV p. 13.

cells.remarks: Issued from Jayapurākoṭṭa. Records the gift of the village of Svaḷpa-Kōmpai in the Khōmbil viṣaya in favour of some Brāhmaṇas belonging to various gōtras, a descendant of Bhaṭṭa Vāsudēva and who belonged to the Jaṭakarṇa gōtra, Vasiṣṭha pravara, Chhāndōga caraṇa and Kauṭhuma sakhā for the merit of the donor and his parents. (1) Śaka 1124 (Jina-

ṇimā), Saptamī;
(2) Śaka 1127-(triksha-
bhūmi-indu), Kārttī-
ka su. 9, gurau, rātri-
dina, śu. 15 = 1206
A.D., January 26.
cells.remarks: Records the genealogies of the Viriyāla and Maḷyāla chiefs commencing from Sūra and Dannaya respectively. cells.place: Another face of the pillar of Śiva, Śiva temple. †
cells.date: Year 13, Kālayukti, Bhādrapada ba. Ekādaśī, Thursday = 1158 A.D., September 1.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of land and a house site by Mahāmaṇḍalēś- vara Ereyamarasa for the god Kēśavadēva, installed by Veppaṇṇaya-nāyaka in the Nakharēśvara temple at Agra- hāra Erigi, for the worship of the god, for maintaining the priest and for the repairs and whitewashing of the temple. Ereyamarasa is described as Amarāvatī paramēś- vārivara. Also records a grant of money from out of the customs accrued from twenty-two towns for Sandhivigrahī (name not given) and supply of flowers on specified occasions by the flower-vendors.

cells.location: Hottal
cells.place: Two sides of a pillar lying in the compound of a dilapidated Śiva temple.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a temple of Śiva called Siddhēś- vara at Kalyāṇapura by Sōmaladēvi, queen of Vikramāditya, a subordinate of the rulers of the Vahni-kula, who were themselves apparently feudatories of the Chālukyas of Kalyāṇa. Also records a gift of money at the rate of a dramma and nisha per village from twenty-four towns to the guru Sōmēśvara in the presence of the preceptor (guru) Chandra- rāśi to god Siddhēśvara. In characters of about the 12th century. See No. 184 below. Published in EP. Ind., Vol. XXXV, pp. 159 ff.

cells.location: Taḍkhal
cells.place: Sculptured slab in the com-pound of the Mallēśvara temple.
cells.date: Śaka 969, Sarvajit, Vaiśākha śu. 3, Wednesday = 1047 A.D., April 1.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the Chālukya family upto Trailōkya-malla and introduces a subordinate chief, Danḍanāyaka Nāgavarma of the Vāji family, whose genealogy also is given. Mentions some history over the last viz. Milla, the lord of the Vindhyas and the Sēvuṇa chief. States that the king, at the time of his performing the Shōḍaśa-mahā-dāna celebrated the marriage of Nāgavarma and gave him the village of Taḍkhal in Sakkarage-30.

cells.place: Sculptured pillar lying in the same com-pound.
cells.date: Śaka 993, Siddhārtha, Pushya ba. 5, Friday, Uttarā-yaṇa samkrānti = 1070 A. D., Decem-ber 24. (The year was current.)
cells.remarks: Records a grant of land made to the Nigaļika-Jimūtavāhana constructed by Danḍanāyaka Kulimayya of the Vāji family at Taḍakal. The grant was made with the consent of the prabhus of Nāyigāve and Taḍakal. Also records a grant of a house grown and land for service to the same community by Danḍanāyaka Nāgavarma, the prabhus of Taḍakal and the mahājanas of the place. A grant of money is also recorded at the end of the inscription.

Out of 70 kāśu was invested to yield 30 kāśu per annum at the rate of a quarter of a dharamā per kāśu per month for paying of the taxes.

cells.remarks: Commences with the praśasti, Vīramē tuṇaiyāyavam etc. Records that, on representation to the officer who was encamping in the temple, the villagers of Kīḻaiyūr, a village in Tiruvēṅkāḍu in Muṉṟaiyūr-nāḍu, in Vērkāḍu-nāḍu, from his camp in the Gaṅgaikoṇḍaśōḻan maṇḍapam at the Tirumayāṉam uḍaiyār temple in Kāñchīpuram, the provision made, originally by a private individual, for the conducting the seven-day festival ending on the day of Tiruvātirai in Āni having been found insufficient, the (the officer) assigned the income from various taxes including Rājadhi-rāja-vīthiyār-irai to the temple and also for feeding the Śrīmahēśvaras attending the festival.

cells.location: Kanavi Shidgêri
cells.place: Slab set up in the Châlukya of Kalyâṇa Jayasimha Siddhesvara temple on the Siddappana- gudda about a mile from the village.
cells.remarks: Lower portion damaged. Records a gift of land, house-site and oil-mill to [samadagi] Râmêsvara-deva at Eluvalli by Mahâmandalēśvara Pâṇḍyadevarsa and his subordinate Kumâra Chauṇḍa. The record contains a preamble praising the family who is said to have belonged to the Kadamba family. The gift was entrusted to Bhaṭō- śaktidēva, the sthânapati of the temple. The composer of the record was Boppa, and Nêmoja engraved it. In charac- ters of about the 12th century.

cells.place: Slab lying near the temple of Bayala Basavappa beside the field of Khāṇōji Kālāl.
cells.date: Saka 1080, Bahudhānya, Kārtika amāvāsī, Sōmavāra, lunar eclipse. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Badly damaged and worn out. Records gifts of land and money probably to a temple by Mahamaṇḍalēśvara Īśvara-dēva. Mentions certain chiefs and his subordinate. The gift was made over to Kalyāṇasaktipaṇḍita. It refers to Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara (Nammīya Gaṅga Permāḍidēva) as governing Eḍeveṭṭe-70 division. Seems to contain an account of the Sinda family. Other details are lost.

cells.place: Hero-stone standing in the shrine of Īśvara within the temple of Basavappa.
cells.date: Śaka 1185 (wrong for 1186), Rākta-kshi, Chaitra su. 10 (?), Sunday = 1294 A. D., March 5.
cells.remarks: Records when Sihgeyab-danāyaka, the Mahāpradhāna of the Hoysala kingdom, raided Hanjūr in the Edavetta country and drove away the cattle. Nālagrabhu śāsana Kālagaunda's battle, disciple (?) of Mūrūjiśādēva, attacked Bīmarasa, brother-in-law of Ereyanga, the Hoysala (?), and died in the fight that ensued after freeing the cattle. The record states that Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kumāra Bommi-dēvarasa was administering the country from his capital at Hosagunda.

cells.remarks: Records a gift to the temple of god Mākālēśvara of Mēgavu built by Mākālēśvaragunda, after worshipping the feet of Agni-bhaṭāraka. Mentions Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Chāvuṇḍa-rāyarasa as governing Banavāsi-12000, and Mahāsāmantādhipati as subordinate to him, Ereyanga Rātapaḷḷi-70 and Mūgunda-12. cells.place: Another slab in the place of Kallēśvara, Kallēśvara temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1087, Paushya, Uttarāyana samkrānti lunar eclipse. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Worn out at the top. Records a gift of income from several taxes by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Īsvaradēva of the Sinda family of Belagutti, to god Mallikārjuna temple at Nidu- nēgila was built by Uroleya Mahādēva. The record gives account of various taxes like aṅka-yaṇḍa, bhotige, the grant of land, garden, oil-mill and income from taxes, to the same god, for worship and offerings as also for feeding the ascetics and students, by Orodeya Mahādēvasāmi with permission of gaudas, heggades and mahajanas of the mēļige of Banavāsi-12000. The gift was made over to the āchārya of Dakshiṇa-Kēdārasvara of Balipura. The latter is said to have been administering a vast area, the details of which are enumerated, from his capital at Haļavura.

cells.place: Slab set up by the side of Paramēśvara temple †
cells.date:
(1) Jagadekamalla [Saka] 1070, Prabhava, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti, Monday, -1174 A.D., December 25; Kārtika ba. 1. The Saka year was current.
(2) Sarvajit, Chaitra su. 1, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti, Monday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records that Kāmagaṅyuḍa, son of Keñchaseṭṭi had the temple of Rāmīśvara built and made a gift of 60 gadyāṇa of Bāṇavāse-nāḍu, and donated a garden and land to the same on the first date, On the same day the Five hundred (merchants) do. also gave (some) dālivōva-daṇḍanāyaka, an officer in charge of the toll-gate, remitted their dues on the taxes. In the next year, Vibbhavu, Kāmagaṅvuṇḍa having passed away, his son Rēcha-gāvuṇḍa renewed the gift with the consent of the chief and (the paṇya)-hiśa-muni of the Pādapōto school on the second date. The inscribed slab was set up by Masaņi-seṭṭi, son of Jakki-seṭṭi. At the time of the second date Sōvidēva of the Kadamba-kula was ruling the Bānavase country. Cf. M.A.R., 1928, p. 77, No. 79.

cells.location: Kembhāvī
cells.place: Pillar in the Rēvaṇa Si-dhēśvara temple.
cells.date: Śaka 976, Jaya, Śrāvaṇa Pushya, Utttarā-yaṇa - saṁkrānti. Probably = 1054 A.D., December 24, Saturday.
cells.remarks: Records the installation of the god Mallikārjuna by Māliyabhanasi, wife of [Mahāmandaleśvara] Rēvarasa and registers a grant of land for the worship of the god, the maintenance of musicians and feeding of ascetics and students studying in the śālai. Mentions a grant of land to Śiva. Also records a supplementary grant of land and māṇeyakkala sāmya of the villages Karadikāl and Kūḍalige situated in Kembhāvi-24 and of Nagaravāra situated in Sagara-300 to the same god, by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rēvarasa. The record was written by Chaṅgādēvayya. Rēvarasa is credited with subduing Mummuṇi Koṅkaṇiga. Noticed in Ep. Ind., Vol. XII, pp. 292-93.

cells.remarks: Jâvûr.—Slab set up near the Râmalinga temple. Châlukya of Kalyāṇa Jagadēkamalla [Jayasimha II] . (1) Śaka 938, Nala, Uttirâyana-saṁkrâ- nti-1016 A.D., December 23, Sun- day=f.d.t. 14. (2) Śaka 940, Bahu- dhânya, Pausha su. 11, Friday, Uttarâyana saṁkrâ- ti. Irregular. Kannada, Nâgari . States that the village Jâvûr together with all the taxes was granted to Manergeyade Chattapayya-nayaka (by the king) on the first date and a copper-plate charter was issued to that effect. Another grant on the second date by Bômayya of Ugrakôthî, made to the god Dîpavali in the temple of Trai- purushadêva was made on the second date by Mahâmanda- lêśvara Jôgapayya who camped at Jâvûr on his way to the military station in Kisukâḍ-70. It records provision of righteous deeds of Chattapayya. Similar grants of money were made by Mahâmandala Bhîmadêvarâsa and other officers in charge of different taxes.
